name: visual
summary: Visual golden tests: each UI scenario is rendered in a known state and compared with a committed screenshot.

scripts.visual: pnpm --dir packages/client-react exec playwright test --config tests/visual/playwright.config.ts
scripts.visual:update: pnpm --dir packages/client-react exec playwright test --config tests/visual/playwright.config.ts --update-snapshots=all

packages/client-react/tests/visual/host/.note: It holds how a scenario's data becomes app state: what the harness is built with, the machines that start with a value, and what is delivered once the UI is on screen.

packages/client-react/tests/visual/visua.note: A width or height a scenario needs now goes on the scenario: `width` and `height` set the viewport of a page.

notes: Every scenario you have is still the whole app, now pictured as a page: the viewport (1920x1080 unless the scenario sets `width` or `height`), with no frame or padding, so anything below the viewport is no longer in the picture unless the scenario sets a larger `height`. Every golden changes once: run `pnpm visual:update` and open each image before you commit it.
A page now defaults to 1080 pixels tall: a scenario that was drawn 720 tall sets `height: 720`.
For `linux-x64`, run the `Update visual goldens` workflow: it uploads the images as an artifact and commits nothing, and its job summary gives the commands.

If you edited `visual.pw.ts` to size the viewport, a scenario's `width` and `height` now do that. Take the update with `--force`, then move anything else you changed from the copy it keeps in `tools/templates/`.

Chromium now starts with `--disable-partial-raster`, so a scenario given up for shading or a flickering list can come back, as a component. If you added that flag to `playwright.config.ts`, `--force` replaced the file and kept no copy: if yours differed by more than that line, `git show HEAD:packages/client-react/tests/visual/playwright.config.ts` has it.
A native control's own text (a `<select>`) still draws two ways on linux-x64: draw its shown value as ordinary text.
`tests/visual/framing.ts` is new and yours: the root width (480), root padding (8) and viewport (1920x1080) a scenario falls back on.

A set of only whole-app pictures is the shape to avoid: picture each component's states first, then a reasonable number of sections, and keep pages for new screens and sizes (AGENTS.md, "The pyramid").

No example scenario, golden or registry is added to your project. To picture components and sections, copy `registry.tsx` from `tools/templates/visual.packages__client-react__tests__visual__registry.tsx.txt` with your own entries, return `render` from `seedScenario` as `tools/templates/visual.packages__client-react__tests__visual__seeding.ts.txt` does, and put the app's theme root in its `Surround`.

The shipped tolerance is now `{ maxDiffPixels: 8, threshold: 0.01 }`: your `tolerance.ts` is kept and keeps working, and the new one is in `tools/templates/visual.packages__client-react__tests__visual__tolerance.ts.txt` to copy from. A scenario may set `strict`, `maxDiffPixels` or `pixelThreshold` only with a `pnpm visual:jitter --scenario <name>` measurement and its cause written beside it.

`pnpm visual:check:styles` joins `gate:fast`: it fails when `packages/client-react/src/main.tsx` imports a stylesheet or font other than `index.css`. Move such an import into `index.css`, the one file the visual host loads.

`pnpm visual:coverage` lists the UI no scenario renders. It adds `vitest`, `@vitest/browser-playwright` and `@vitest/coverage-v8` to `packages/client-react`; the `pnpm -r update` command under "Next" puts them on one version, which Vitest needs.

A new project's starter now draws in Inter, from woff2 files in `packages/client-react/src/fonts/` declared with `@font-face` in `index.css`. Your project keeps its own fonts, and nothing in your goldens changes. In the pinned container on linux-x64, `system-ui` draws no bold: to have bold there, serve a face of your own the same way, in `index.css`, which the visual host loads.

The example goldens are redrawn in Inter, and `price-list-stale` is a new example section whose row goes stale on the host's clock (`stalePrices`). Neither is added to your project; the templates of `scenarios.ts` and `tolerance.ts` (its comments only) changed, and "Yours to change" shows how.
